pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/oauth.rs:105 token_endpoint_request POSTs client_secret via SHARED_HTTP (no SSRF-safe resolver, default redirect following) to a token_url that is caller data (oauth.rs:2073) or a dependency response (discovery.token_endpoint, oauth.rs:2068); the repo own SSRF_SAFE_HTTP (src-tauri/core/src/http_clients.rs:27) exists for exactly this and is unused here - unchanged since the 2026-10-03 verdict

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/oauth.rs:1205 validate_issuer_url judges only literal-IP hosts, then discover_oidc fetches the name via SHARED_HTTP (oauth.rs:1295) - a second, unbound resolution, and the discovered token_endpoint (oauth.rs:2068) is never judged at all
src/lib/bindings/CreateCredentialInput.ts:15 oauthSessionRef: the command layer merges OAuth tokens server-side, token material never crosses IPC
src-tauri/core/src/models/credential.rs:40 serde skip_serializing + ts(skip) on encrypted_data: the webview shape has no column for the sealed value
src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/oauth.rs:1295 the error caller is the local operator UI of a one-operator desktop install - a trust boundary owned on both sides, which the technique exempts
